symptom: Localized VII pages have distinct locale-prefixed URLs and self canonicals, but several omit og:url or expose the unprefixed Hebrew route as the social sharing URL.
expected_behavior: Every Hebrew, English, Russian and French page exposes a social sharing URL for the same locale and route as the current page.
environment: Public VII production at https://vii.spaplus.co on 2026-10-24 and local branch plan/vii-continuous-quality-20261023.

steps: Open French hourly, spa, business, guides, gift-card and discover place routes.
Inspect the current URL, canonical link, hreflang family and og:url metadata.
Compare the locale represented by each address.
reproduction.evidence: The completed public report qa-reports/comprehensive-public-post-language-20261024/comprehensive-1792806588955.json records missing social URLs and social URLs that point from French pages to unprefixed Hebrew paths.

observations.observation: Locale-prefixed public routes, self canonicals and hreflang families already exist.
observations.evidence: The multilingual production audit reached /en, /ru and /fr routes and did not classify the sampled URLs or canonicals as missing locale identity.

observations.observation: Several page-level metadata generators omit openGraph.url or hardcode an unprefixed route.
observations.evidence: Source inspection of app/hourly/page.tsx, app/spas/page.tsx, app/business/page.tsx, app/guides/page.tsx, app/gift-card/page.tsx and dynamic place metadata before the repair.

hypotheses.mechanism: Page-level metadata overrides either omit openGraph.url or hardcode a Hebrew unprefixed path instead of deriving it from the request locale.
hypotheses.prediction: Localized routing and canonicals remain correct while og:url is missing or points to the Hebrew route on only the affected page families.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare public URL and canonical identity with page-level metadata source and emitted og:url across the affected route families.
hypotheses.result: Supported: the locale route and canonical were distinct, while the exact affected generators omitted or hardcoded openGraph.url.

hypotheses.mechanism: The application has no unique locale routing, so all metadata necessarily resolves to one shared URL.
hypotheses.prediction: French, English and Russian requests would lack locale-prefixed URLs, self canonicals and hreflang alternates.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect the public localized request URL, canonical and hreflang family independently of og:url.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: unique locale-prefixed routes, self canonicals and hreflang alternates are present; the defect is limited to social metadata generation.

fix.change: Derive canonical and openGraph.url from the active request locale for the shared root, listings, gift card, guides, business and dynamic place families.
fix.evidence: The focused metadata and multilingual suites passed 14 of 14 checks, and pnpm build completed successfully after the repair.

affected_family: Root pages in all four locales

regression_checks.check: Root, business, listing, content and dynamic place metadata derive canonical and og:url from the active locale.
regression_checks.evidence: node --test tests/localized-share-metadata.test.mjs tests/localized-root-hydration.test.mjs tests/multilingual-visual-qa.test.mjs passed 14 of 14.

regression_checks.check: Production candidate still compiles and emits the complete route family.
regression_checks.evidence: pnpm build completed successfully with manifestsAgree=true and 217 RSC references.

remaining_unknowns: Exact production metadata remains unchanged until an explicitly authorized release is published and rechecked.
authorization_boundary: Repair and verify safe in-scope code defects locally; do not publish without explicit release authorization and do not invent missing localized business content.
